The purchaser is likely to prevail because he acquired an easement by necessity or implied grant that was not extinguished when the man previously owned both properties. Although the merger doctrine applies while one person holds dominant and servient estates, it does not automatically eliminate a recorded right-of-way if the land is later severed in a way that separates ownership of the two parcels again. Consequently, the man's erection of a barricade to block access violates the purchaser's valid property interest established by the original deed and subsequent severance.

CONFIDENCE: 85
